originalTitle: Bullets that killed two at Seattle food festival do not match teen shooter’s gun, police say
summary: Police link shooting to gang violence but have not said who might have fired bullets that killed bystanders on Sunday
content: Bullets that fatally struck two bystanders during a shootout at a Seattle food festival last weekend do not appear to have come from the gun that a 15-year-old arrested at the scene was firing, police said in court documents filed on Wednesday. The teen sprayed an untraceable “ghost gun” into a crowd, authorities say. Preliminary ballistics testing did not match the bullets recovered from the deceased bystanders to that weapon. Police have linked the shooting to gang violence. Shell casings found at the scene on Sunday indicate four weapons were fired. “We have small groups that appear to be at odds with each other, and in our city 0.01% of the population is connected to 52% of our shootings,” Seattle police chief Shon Barnes said at a news conference on Monday. A 19-year-old suspect was shot and killed at the scene. Police have been trying to identify at least one other person involved in the shooting. They have not indicated who might have fired the bullets that killed the bystanders. In the crossfire, at least four other bystanders were wounded, including a two-year-old boy. Videos posted to social media showed a chaotic scene, with swarms of people running for safety as shots are heard in the distance. The King county prosecutor’s office has charged the 15-year-old with first-degree assault with a firearm enhancement and unlawful possession of a handgun by someone under 18. Prosecutors are seeking for his case to be moved to adult court. If convicted in juvenile court, he could face two and a half years in juvenile detention. In adult court, a conviction would come with a penalty of about eight to 10 years in prison, and another possible five years for the firearm enhancement.
chineseTitle: 警方称，西雅图美食节上造成两人死亡的子弹与青少年射手的枪不符
chineseSummary: 警方将枪击事件与帮派暴力联系起来，但没有透露周日是谁发射的子弹杀死了旁观者
chineseContent: 警方在周三提交的法庭文件中称，上周末西雅图美食节的枪战中，两名旁观者被击中身亡的子弹似乎并非来自现场被捕的一名 15 岁男子所用的枪。当局称，这名青少年向人群喷射了一把无法追踪的“幽灵枪”。初步弹道测试与从已故旁观者身上找到的子弹与该武器不匹配。警方将枪击事件与帮派暴力联系起来。周日现场发现的弹壳表明有四件武器被发射。西雅图警察局长肖恩·巴恩斯 (Shon Barnes) 在周一的新闻发布会上表示：“我们有一些看似相互矛盾的小团体，在我们城市，0.01% 的人口与 52% 的枪击事件有关。”一名 19 岁嫌疑人当场被枪杀。警方一直在试图确认至少一名参与枪击事件的人的身份。他们没有指出谁可能发射了杀死旁观者的子弹。在交火中，至少有四名旁观者受伤，其中包括一名两岁男孩。社交媒体上发布的视频显示，现场一片混乱，远处传来枪声，成群结队的人纷纷逃命。金县检察官办公室对这名 15 岁的男子提出一级攻击罪，罪名是使用枪支增强以及 18 岁以下人士非法持有手枪。检察官正在寻求将他的案件移交成人法庭审理。如果在少年法庭被定罪，他可能面临两年半的少年拘留。在成人法庭，一旦定罪，将被判处约八到十年监禁，并可能因枪支升级而被判处五年徒刑。
whyItMatters: 这条信息属于全球新闻信号，适合用于观察外部环境、政策变化、地缘风险和市场情绪。
